title: Daily Routines & Present Simple
topic: Everyday habits, time expressions, and Present Simple
instructions: Read each question carefully. Circle the best answer or write clearly on the lines provided.

questions.text: Leo ___ his teeth every morning after breakfast.
My sister usually ___ (take) the bus to school at 7:30 AM.
We use 'does' in questions with 'he', 'she', or 'it' (Example: Does she like coffee?).
Match each morning action with the object you use.
Write two things you usually do after dinner on weekdays.
questions.answer: Example answers: I do my homework. / I help wash the dishes and watch TV.

questions.text: Write 3–4 sentences describing your favorite weekend morning.
questions.answer: Check for Present Simple verbs (wake up, eat, play), time words (at 9:00, after breakfast), and capital letters.

title: Irregular Past Simple Check
topic: Past tense forms, negatives, and short weekend recount
instructions: Complete all sections carefully. Remember the difference between affirmative verbs and 'did / didn't' questions.

questions.text: Yesterday we ___ a delicious seafood lunch near the harbor.
Sorry I missed your call — I ___ (leave) my phone at home.
They ___ (not / go) to the cinema because it started raining.
In the sentence 'Did you saw the movie last night?', the verb 'saw' is grammatically correct.
Match each base verb with its correct Past Simple form.
Rewrite this sentence as a Past Simple question: 'Maya visited Kyoto last spring.'
questions.answer: Did Maya visit Kyoto last spring?

title: Food, Quantities & Café Dialogues
topic: Countable/uncountable nouns and polite restaurant requests
titleText: At the Café: Quantities & Polite Requests
instructions: Choose the right quantifier or write polite customer phrases for each café situation.

questions.text: How ___ spoons of honey would you like in your tea?
There isn't ___ milk left in the fridge, so we should buy a carton.
Nouns like 'bread', 'rice', and 'advice' are uncountable in standard English.
Match each café phrase with the person most likely to say it.

pairs.left: Could I have the bill, please?
Would you like sparkling or still?

questions.text: Make this order more polite: 'Give me a toasted cheese sandwich and lemonade.'
questions.answer: Could I have / I'd like a toasted cheese sandwich and a lemonade, please?

questions.text: Write a short 4-line dialogue between a customer and a café server.
questions.answer: Include a greeting, one polite order ('I'd like / Could I have'), one follow-up question from the server, and thank you.

title: Travel, Airports & City Survival
topic: Airport vocabulary, modal advice, and situational writing
instructions: Imagine you are traveling abroad. Answer each travel item clearly.

questions.text: Passengers must show their ___ before walking through the boarding gate.
If your flight is delayed by three hours, you ___ check the departures screen for a new gate.
When traveling internationally, 'carry-on luggage' must always be checked into the cargo hold.
Match each airport sign or word to its meaning.

pairs.right: Area where you collect checked suitcases
Desk where travelers declare restricted goods
Short stop between two connecting flights

questions.text: Give two polite questions to ask a stranger when you get lost looking for a subway station.
questions.answer: e.g., 'Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the nearest subway station?' / 'Is this the right way to...?'

questions.text: Plan a one-day city itinerary for a visiting friend (morning, lunch, afternoon, evening).
questions.answer: Evaluate clear sequencing markers (First, After lunch, In the afternoon), logical landmarks, and travel vocabulary.

title: Green Energy & Planet Quiz
instructions: Review renewable energy concepts and explain your ideas in clear English sentences.

questions.text: Which of these energy sources relies on underground heat rather than wind or sunlight?
Unlike fossil fuels, renewable sources such as wind and solar do not run ___ over human timescales.
Composting kitchen food scraps helps reduce methane emissions in landfills.
Match each sustainability term with its real-world example.

pairs.right: Bringing your own refillable water bottle
Turning clean glass jars into pantry storage
Sorting aluminum cans into the blue bin

questions.text: Explain one practical challenge of relying 100% on solar power alone.
questions.answer: Sunlight varies at night and during cloudy weather, so energy storage (batteries) or grid backup is needed.

questions.text: What single change could your school or neighborhood make next month to cut plastic waste?
questions.answer: Look for a specific proposal, one supporting reason, and a realistic step students/neighbors could take.

title: Connectors & Critical Writing
topic: Contrast/cause linkers, register refinement, and structured paragraphs
instructions: Pay close attention to punctuation (commas, semicolons) and formal register when completing each task.

questions.text: ___ the heavy rain throughout the afternoon, the outdoor science exhibition attracted record crowds.
The software update improved battery life; ___, some older devices still experience minor lag.
'Although' can be followed directly by a noun phrase like 'Although the bad weather, we went out.'
Match each linking expression to its rhetorical function.
Combine these two ideas using 'Even though': 'Remote work reduces commuting time. Many employees still miss casual office chats.'
questions.answer: Even though remote work reduces commuting time, many employees still miss casual office chats.

questions.text: Should public libraries extend opening hours until 10:00 PM? Write a concise one-paragraph argument using at least two formal connectors.
questions.answer: Clear topic stance, 1–2 supporting points (students, evening workers), 1 counterargument or cost point, and 2+ accurate connectors (However, Moreover, Consequently).
